places.warn: Fifteen census villages named Hadmatiya were found across Rajkot, Morbi, Jamnagar, Devbhumi Dwarka, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Junagadh, Gir Somnath, Sabarkantha and Mahisagar districts. None is in Surendranagar or Anand, so the travel route does not disambiguate it. The Tankara (Morbi district) candidate is the most plausible on geography alone, but that is inference, not evidence. Both Wikipedia articles titled Hadmatiya contradict themselves on district. Do not pin this until a Gujarati primary source names the district. OpenStreetMap holds only three nodes of the name in Gujarat — Hadmatiya in Paddhari taluka, Rajkot district (22.43352, 70.48005), which also has a railway station of that name on the Rajkot–Wankaner line; a Hadmatiya at 24.64183, 72.68557 in the north; and a Hadmatia locality at 20.71343, 70.87421. None of the three is attested as His Hadmatiya, and the census count is far higher than three, so this only narrows where to look next.

places.evidence: Named in the VS 1952 travel entry.

On the evening of Aso Vad Ekam, VS 1952 — 22 October 1896, the day after Sharad Purnima — He composed the Shri Atmasiddhi Shastra, all 142 verses, at a single sitting, at Sobhagbhai's request, with Ambalalbhai holding the lantern. Revisited in VS 1957 (1900–01). This is, by most reckonings, the most significant single location of His life.
places.warn: Wikipedia's Atma Siddhi article cites 31-3-1888. That is the date of the underlying letter to Lalluji Maharaj, not the composition date. Do not conflate them.

places.warn: Newly identified in this edition. A village named Rajpur sits in the Khambhat taluka roster inside the 'Ralaj-Rajpura' gram panchayat, paired with Ralej and neighbouring Metpur — precisely the Ralej–Vadva–Khambhat cluster of the same travel entry. Population 519. No gazetteer publishes its coordinates, so it is identified but not yet pinned. This is not the Rajmandir Ashram site, and not Rajpur in Barwani, MP. Village-directory and census listings add that Rajpur lies about 9 km from Khambhat town, covers 2,444.88 hectares and carries pincode 388640 — a constraint tight enough to identify the village on the ground, but still not a published coordinate.

places.evidence: Four documented visits: first in VS 1952 (1895–96) for ten days; again in Vaishakh VS 1953 (April–May 1897) staying with Sobhagbhai; a three-month retreat beginning Magshar Sud 2, VS 1955 (Nov/Dec 1898); and a further twelve days later that year. On a giant rock He recited the first gatha of the third chapter of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra and the whole Dravyasangrah to seven monks, and declared the slab Pudhavi Sheela — Siddhsheela, the abode of the liberated.
places.warn: The Viharbhuvan's own history page dates it to VS 1966 (1909–10) and states it was built on the original rock. The rock is a lifetime site; the building over it is not. The paduka, the Sumatinath idol and the paintings are all later installations. Separately, SRMD's 2023 Dharmayatra report names four further Idar sites — Mahakaleshwar, Chandaneshwar and Khokhanath Mahadev and Ramdwar Mandir — as places where He performed spiritual practices, but gives no lifetime detail; these are 2023 portrait installations at claimed sites.
